key_insight: A NURBS-based level set framework enables robust, CAD-compatible topology optimization of Kirchhoff–Love shells using volume-based shape derivatives from the speed method.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports lightweight shell design under uncertain loads and material properties while preserving compatibility with CAD/CAM workflows.
method: Use isogeometric analysis for multi-patch shells with non-matching meshes.
Compute volume-based shape derivatives and biharmonic descent directions without local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming.
Represent uncertainty with Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian random fields.
evidence_signal: Numerical single- and multi-patch examples reproduce literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined isogeometric approaches, according to the abstract.
watch_item: Monte Carlo sampling may increase optimization cost; the abstract does not quantify runtime savings or sampling convergence.
paper_title: Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
